About me

From the media side and the brand side.

I have launched international brands in Kosovo, built a tiered loyalty program, taken an e‑commerce brand into Albania, and put brands on national TV through commercials and sponsorship.

Today I lead marketing for eight brands at KES Group across e‑commerce, automotive, furniture, logistics, fitness and hospitality. I use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini in my day to day work.

Marketing and admissions, November 2026 to January 2027

The first 90 days

A plan for turning the school's media, story and systems into enrolled families.

November

Build

Listen to the school, the agency and every media partner. Put HubSpot and WhatsApp Business live. Answer every enquiry in under five minutes.

December

Ignite

Launch “See for yourself” across TV, radio, portals and social. Celebrate Finland's Independence Day. Open Koonta to visiting families.

January

Convert

Open Day, scholarships and mid year entry. Follow up every family met in December. First quarterly report to the Chairman's Office.

One principle runs through all three months: every campaign is tied to enquiries, and every enquiry is followed through to enrolment.

PISA 2025 put education quality at the top of Kosovo's agenda.

Results published 8 September 2026 place Kosovo 8th from the bottom. Parents, media and the ministry will debate this for months. The school can add a constructive, expert voice.

“The #1 education system in the world” is now easy to challenge.

Finland scored well above the OECD average, while Estonia, Canada and the United Kingdom scored higher. The Finnish link stays the school's great asset. The message should move from a ranking to proof families can see.

Sources: Ministry of Education via Koha, Epoka e Re; Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture, 8 September 2026; OECD

Growth will come from Kosovar families and IMPACT.

The international niche is smallQSI International School of Kosovo reports 175 students and 36 faculty in 2026. International families matter, but they are a focused segment.
Kosovar families are the volumeFamilies in Prishtina and beyond who want an international future for their children, in English, with Cambridge.
IMPACT opens the middle marketFinnish practice in Albanian at a more affordable price reaches families that never considered a private school.

Source: US Department of State, QSI Kosovo 2026 Fact Sheet

Five things to fix

1Media without a systemNo measurable path from an advert to an enrolled family.
2A promise, not proofThe #1 ranking claim is fragile after PISA 2025.
3Two products, one voiceThe English programme and IMPACT speak to different families.
4Content without storiesKoonta, University Bridge and EinsteinAI are unique and under told.
5No road for relocating familiesEmbassies, organisations and employers have no dedicated path.
02Direction

From “#1 in the world” to “See for yourself”.

A school families are invited to see.

Every piece of communication ends with an invitation: a visit, a trial day, an Open Day, an open Koonta. Parents choosing an international school move from awareness to interest, evaluation and finally a trial, so the trial becomes the centre of every campaign.

Source: Council of International Schools, international school parent choice

What a child does here that they do nowhere else in Kosovo

KoontaThe town where your child learns to work, vote and save.
University BridgeUniversity starts in grade 11.
Recognised abroadTop 10 in the world, Cambridge and CIS: other people's verdict.
Finnish teachersThe people behind the method, in front of the camera.

03The foundation

One record per family, measured at every stage.

The admissions system goes live in the first two weeks. Without it, every euro on air is lost. Tap a stage to see what happens there.

Under five minutesIn school hours, a real answer. Outside them, a useful one. Firms that reply within an hour are about seven times likelier to qualify an enquiry.
Every channel codedEach TV spot, radio slot, article and post carries its own WhatsApp keyword or link, so we know who sent each family.
Nothing falls throughAutomatic follow up within 24 hours of a visit, with a short film of the classroom the parent saw.

Source: Harvard Business Review, lead response research

Built in November: the system, in six parts

One front doorWeb form, WhatsApp, phone, DMs and events all land in HubSpot with their source.

WhatsApp Business for admissionsFirst reply within a minute; an AI assistant answers common questions and books visits.

Clear stagesSeven stages in HubSpot, each one measured.

Monthly dashboardEnquiries by channel, cost per enquiry, cost per enrolled family, response time, conversion.

The school owns its dataAd accounts, tracking and campaign data stay with the school; partners get access.

Every automation documentedWhat it does, who approves it, what happens when it fails.

04The channels

Six channels, each with a clear way to respond.

05Execution

Build, ignite, convert.

Month by month, with the numbers that decide what continues. Tick items off to follow the plan.

Targets set together after two weeks of real data

Response timeUnder 5 minutes in school hours
Enquiries by channelTV, radio, portal, social, event, referral
Cost per enquiryBy channel, every month
Cost per enrolled familyThe number budget decisions follow
Stage conversionEnquiry through to enrolment
Airtime used100%, no minute returned

Reported monthly to the Head of School and quarterly to the Chairman's Office, in numbers. Families at risk of leaving are tracked from day one.

Evidence decides where the money goes

  • November: small tests in every channel
  • December and January: weekly shifts to the lowest cost per attended visit
  • Every decision taken from the dashboard
  • Any software that stops justifying its cost is withdrawn
The ranking claimLead with proof and external recognition instead.
A new way of workingTraining for the team starts in week one.
Schedules changeEvery slot confirmed with each partner first.
Hiring takes timeThe agency covers production until the videographer starts.
